body:
Product attack: do not let the architecture prove itself merely by working. Each costly feature needs an incremental value test against a simpler baseline.

1) Two-site Stage security. Experiment: hostile canary audit plus moderated setup test comparing separate-origin build with a single-origin strict public projection build. KEEP only if public/private display remains central and separate-origin setup success is >=90% unassisted after one rehearsal, while canary leakage is exactly 0. KILL/DEFER separate registrable domains if the simpler server-projected Stage also yields 0-byte private leakage and improves successful setup by >=10 percentage points; preserve logical DTO/gateway separation regardless.

2) Second-device mirror control. Experiment: 10-15 target presenters perform fresh pairing in an actual mirrored classroom against baseline 'present from extended display / no private console.' KEEP if >=80% pair and reach ready state within 90s without facilitator, p95 control latency <=500ms, reconnect recovery <=2s, and >=60% prefer/reuse it. KILL productized pairing if <70% complete within 2 minutes, >10% expose private UI, or median perceived setup burden >4/7. Then mirror becomes public-Stage-only with printed/voice/manual fallback.

3) Live public evidence. A/B normal slides vs pre-approved evidence vs live candidates. Public live publishing is gated on candidate precision, not recall: false-SUPPORT <=1%, wrong numeric/date/entity publication =0 in test corpus, p95 eligible-candidate latency <=5s, and >=30% of candidates are actually used in relevant Q&A without increasing interruptions. KILL automatic/live-public path if approval adds >2s median per event, causes >1 extra presenter interruption per 10-minute talk, or trust/relevance improves <0.5 on a 7-point scale over pre-approved cards. Keep live search presenter-private.

4) Automatic extended placement. Compare Tier-1 auto placement against explicit manual instructions after one rehearsal. KEEP only if auto success >=95% on supported Chrome/Edge machines and reduces median setup by >=20s with no privacy incident. KILL as marketed feature if permission/popup/topology failures exceed 5% or manual success is already >=90% within 60s. It remains progressive enhancement only.

5) Approval cognitive load. Instrument candidate arrival->view->approve/reject, missed slide changes, presenter gaze loss, speech pauses, and NASA-TLX single-item effort. Gate public approval UX on median decision <=2s, p90 <=5s, <=1 induced pause per 10 minutes, and workload increase <1/7 vs pre-approved baseline. Otherwise use pre-show approvals or team-member operator.

6) Split attention. Within-subject audience test: slides only vs one presenter-triggered card vs rotating/multiple cards. Require comprehension or source-recall improvement >=10% without >5% decline in core-slide recall. KILL persistent/multi-card/auto-rotation if core recall declines >=5%, glance switching rises without comprehension gain, or >=20% report distraction. Default one card, short reveal, no auto-rotation, immediate stale on slide change.

7) Whole-MVP setup gate. From signed-out/fresh browser to audience-ready: >=85% first-attempt completion unassisted, median <=3 min, p90 <=5 min across extend and mirror. If either mode misses, stop adding AI; fix or narrow that mode first.

Strong recommendation: MVP promise should be secure two-mode delivery of pre-approved evidence. Treat live public evidence and automatic placement as separately earned options, not architectural prerequisites.
summary: Falsifiable product experiments and kill thresholds
